> Two asks from my side:

> - If Exhibit E drives billing precedence, do we want a one-line fallback that says billing cadence governs in case of conflict?

Diego / Kimberly — attaching redlined orderform and Exhibit E workbook. See high-level notes below and inline comments in the doc: Skylark_Orderform_v3_redline.docx; ExhibitE_coverage.xlsx.

Top-level legal notes:
- Section 4.2 (Term & Renewal): propose explicit language: "Initial term is 18 months; any capacity increases during the term will be documented in an executed order form; such increases do not extend the Initial Term unless agreed in writing by both parties." This prevents the uplift from automatically restarting the term.
- Auto-renewal: change to opt-in auto-renewal only for enterprise customers with 60-day notice; include a one-time right for vendor to propose renewal pricing adjustments tied to capacity increases.
- Billing vs usage precedence: recommend a fallback sentence: "In the event of any inconsistency between Exhibit E and the billing schedule in the Order Form, the billing schedule shall govern for invoicing purposes; Exhibit E governs operational allocation of capacity."
- Credits & termination: add a limited right to terminate for material breach (including failure to pay) with a pro-rata credit for unused pre-paid capacity; exclude termination for routine usage variance.
- Data & audit: procurement asked for audit clause — we support a standard SOC2 evidence delivery timeline; include a redline referencing existing SOC2 attestation link.

Attachments below contain inline comments where I flagged language that could create long-term precedence risk (e.g., blanket "no refunds" phrasing). DocuSign template link at the bottom of the Order Form (docu_sign_request_78294.link.txt).

Will push a cleaned version to the shared doc and add comment threads for the KM/Diego sync. If we need counsel input on the SLA uplift impact, I can escalate to LegalOps.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
